reference: Documented Linux inotify event semantics and the Bash watch API. Synchronous small private file operations generate fixed create/modify/ignored records. Contract assertions compare event names and the descriptor returned by add, not metadata alone; no GNU CLI parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash identifies bashinotify as a builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented subcommands and persistent-fd description.
Bash help exposes the documented mask names.
Bash help exposes wait timeout, count, and output-line contract details.
Private add/WDVAR/mask parsing, synchronous create/modify events, empty polling, bounded waits, event count, rm/ignored and close/reinitialization.
exclusions: Rename cookies, coalescing, unmount/overflow and fault injection are unqualified; no system setting or host watch is used.

cases.purpose: Use Bash's type -t builtin to verify that the loadable is registered as a Bash builtin, without invoking an inotify operation.
Check that Bash help includes the documented add, rm, wait, and close subcommands and states that the inotify fd is retained across calls.
cases.script:
doc=$(help bashinotify)
if [[ $doc == *"Filesystem watch via inotify(7)."* && $doc == *"bashinotify add PATH MASK"* && $doc == *"bashinotify rm WD"* && $doc == *"bashinotify wait [-t MS] [-n N]"* && $doc == *"bashinotify close"* && $doc == *"Single inotify fd held in loadable state across calls."* ]]; then
  printf 'help:commands-and-state-present\n'
else
  printf 'help:commands-or-state-missing\n'
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Check the advertised comma-separated add mask vocabulary against the embedded bashinotify help contract.
cases.script:
doc=$(help bashinotify)
if [[ $doc == *"MASK is comma-separated:"* && $doc == *modify* && $doc == *create* && $doc == *delete* && $doc == *attrib* && $doc == *"move move-from"* && $doc == *move-to* && $doc == *open* && $doc == *access* && $doc == *close-write* && $doc == *close-nowrite* && $doc == *delete-self* && $doc == *move-self* && $doc == *unmount* && $doc == *all* ]]; then
  printf 'help:documented-mask-vocabulary-present\n'
else
  printf 'help:documented-mask-vocabulary-missing\n'
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Check that help documents the wait output shape and both timeout and event-count options, including the nonblocking zero-timeout meaning.
cases.script:
doc=$(help bashinotify)
if [[ $doc == *"bashinotify wait [-t MS] [-n N]"* && $doc == *"read pending events; one line"* && $doc == *"WD EVENT_NAMES NAME"* && $doc == *"-t MS: timeout (0=no wait, default=block)"* && $doc == *"-n N:"* && $doc == *"max events to emit per call"* ]]; then
  printf 'help:wait-contract-present\n'
else
  printf 'help:wait-contract-missing\n'
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Watch a private directory, bind the descriptor in the current shell and observe a synchronous create event. No timing-based producer is used.
cases.script:
mkdir watched
bashinotify add watched ' create , modify ' wd
[[ $wd =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
printf 'small\n' > watched/child
bashinotify wait -t 0 > events
mapfile -t rows < events
[[ ${#rows[@]} == 2 && ${rows[0]} == "$wd create child" && ${rows[1]} == "$wd modify child" ]]
bashinotify close
printf 'create and modify; bound descriptor\n'

cases.purpose: A bounded wait emits at most one event and a zero-timeout wait emits nothing when the watched directory has no pending events.
cases.script:
mkdir watched
bashinotify add watched create wd
bashinotify wait -t 0 > empty-events
[[ ! -s empty-events ]]
: > watched/child
bashinotify wait -t 50 -n 1 > events
mapfile -t rows < events
[[ ${#rows[@]} == 1 && ${rows[0]} == "$wd create child" ]]
bashinotify close
printf 'empty poll and one event\n'

cases.purpose: Removing a private watch emits ignored, close is idempotent, and a new add works after close.
cases.script:
mkdir watched
bashinotify add watched create wd
bashinotify rm "$wd"
bashinotify wait -t 0 > events
mapfile -t rows < events
[[ ${#rows[@]} == 1 && ${rows[0]} == "$wd ignored" ]]
bashinotify close
bashinotify close
bashinotify add watched create next
[[ $next =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
bashinotify close
printf 'removed, closed, reinitialized\n'

cases.purpose: Two distinct synchronous file creations must remain observable across two -n 1 calls, one event per call.
cases.script:
mkdir watched
bashinotify add watched create wd
: > watched/first
: > watched/second
bashinotify wait -t 0 -n 1 > first-events
bashinotify wait -t 0 -n 1 > second-events
mapfile -t first < first-events
mapfile -t second < second-events
[[ ${#first[@]} == 1 && ${first[0]} == "$wd create first" ]]
[[ ${#second[@]} == 1 && ${second[0]} == "$wd create second" ]]
bashinotify close
printf 'both events retained\n'

cases.purpose: A zero event limit consumes nothing; two bounded subsequent waits still receive the synchronous private creations in order.
cases.script:
mkdir watched
bashinotify add watched create wd
: > watched/first
: > watched/second
bashinotify wait -t 0 -n 0 > zero
[[ ! -s zero ]]
bashinotify wait -t 0 -n 1 > first
bashinotify wait -t 20 -n 1 > second
[[ $(<first) == "$wd create first" && $(<second) == "$wd create second" ]]
bashinotify close
printf "zero and timed waits retain events\n"
cases.stdout: zero and timed waits retain events

cases.purpose: Closing a private watch discards its buffered remainder before a new instance receives a different private creation.
cases.script:
mkdir watched
bashinotify add watched create wd
: > watched/old1
: > watched/old2
bashinotify wait -t 0 -n 1 > old
bashinotify close
bashinotify add watched create wd
: > watched/new
bashinotify wait -t 0 > current
[[ $(<current) == "$wd create new" ]]
bashinotify close
printf "reopened watch has only new events\n"
cases.stdout: reopened watch has only new events
